entry.summary: A tourist visa on arrival for tourism and leisure, up to 120 days, single entry.
entry.max_stay: 120 days; no on-shore extension and no change of visa status in Vanuatu
entry.pre_arrival: A booking with an accredited tourism facility, or a letter of support from family or friends if staying privately, and a return ticket.
entry.passport_validity: At least 6 months from the date of entry.
entry.other: Employment, commercial or business activity is not permitted on a tourist visa.

laws.rule: Fines and imprisonment for drug offences, even small amounts.
Supermarkets and similar outlets can't sell alcohol from midday Saturday to 7 am Monday; clubs, bars and hotels can still serve.
Strict customs and biosecurity rules on food, weapons and obscene material (Customs and Inland Revenue, Biosecurity Vanuatu).
Drive on an Australian licence for up to 3 months, then a local licence. Digital licences may not be accepted.
Employment, commercial or business activity is not permitted on a tourist visa.

culture-and-protocol.dress_and_conduct: Modest dress and behaviour. Same-sex relationships are legal but not widely accepted; avoid public affection. Vanuatu Tourism Office: villages are on customary land. Arrange visits through a guide, ask before entering homes, nakamals or gardens and before photographing children, pay any custom fees, and respect tabu areas.
culture-and-protocol.cultural_authority: Custom land and places are under the authority of their custom owners: ask locally, through your host or the village chief, before visiting.
culture-and-protocol.note: Read from the Australian Government's description of local customs.

festivals.what: Naghol (land diving), Pentecost: a custom ceremony tied to the yam harvest, usually April to June, with days set locally. Vanuatu Tourism lists visitor events with fees; confirm dates and fees with the operator.

closures: Weekend: supermarkets and similar shops can't sell alcohol from midday Saturday to 7 am Monday (clubs, bars and hotels can still serve).
protocol_notes: Naghol belongs to the Pentecost communities. Go through a community-linked operator, follow your hosts on where to stand and what to film, and expect custom fees.
culture-cycles.note: Festivals and community closures are still to be read from each place's own tourism office and communities.

tourism.route: Tourist visa on arrival (up to 120 days)
tourism.detail: Tourism only: no employment, commercial or business activity on a tourist visa.

meetings.route: Business visa (single entry 3 months, or multiple entry 10 months)
meetings.detail: Business needs the business visa; the tourist visa doesn't allow business activity.

conference.route: Business visa (single entry 3 months, or multiple entry 10 months)
conference.detail: Business needs the business visa; the tourist visa doesn't allow business activity.

unpaid-speaking.route: Business visa (single entry 3 months, or multiple entry 10 months) or Business visa for short-term employment, with a temporary work permit from the Labour Department and the employer's letter
unpaid-speaking.detail: Speaking at a business conference fits a business visit; other speaking may count as work.
unpaid-speaking.next: Ask the Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services.

paid-speaking.route: Specialist Skill visa (sponsored, up to two weeks) or Short-Term Employment visa
paid-speaking.detail: Sponsored specialist work up to two weeks uses the Specialist Skill visa; longer skilled work up to six months uses the Short-Term Employment visa.

book-launch.route: Business visa for short-term employment, with a temporary work permit from the Labour Department and the employer's letter
book-launch.detail: Paid work needs a temporary work permit from the Labour Department plus the business visa.
book-launch.next: Ask the Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services.

ai-teaching.route: Specialist Skill visa (sponsored, up to two weeks) or Short-Term Employment visa
ai-teaching.detail: Sponsored specialist work up to two weeks uses the Specialist Skill visa; longer skilled work up to six months uses the Short-Term Employment visa.

remote-work.detail: No remote-work rule was found on the official pages.
remote-work.next: Ask the Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services.

entrepreneur.route: Foreign Investment Registration Certificate, then business licence
entrepreneur.detail: Foreign investors need a FIRC from VFIPA first (online, 1 to 7 working days, business plan and police clearance), then a business licence from Customs and Inland Revenue (VT5,000 to VT20,000).

trade.route: Business visa (single entry 3 months, or multiple entry 10 months)
trade.detail: Meetings and negotiation are business visits; delivering work is not.
trade.next: Ask the Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services.

artist.route: Specialist Skill visa (sponsored, up to two weeks) or Short-Term Employment visa
artist.detail: Sponsored specialist work up to two weeks uses the Specialist Skill visa; longer skilled work up to six months uses the Short-Term Employment visa.

mixed-mission.detail: Visitor, business and work routes each cover different parts.
mixed-mission.next: Ask the Vanuatu Department of Immigration and Passport Services.

filming.route: Business visa (single entry 3 months, or multiple entry 10 months) plus a Vanuatu Cultural Centre (Vanuatu Kaljoral Senta) film permit
filming.detail: Filming is a named business-visa purpose and needs the Cultural Centre's film permit. Custom land and kastom stories need the custom owners' permission too.
filming.next: Apply to the Vanuatu Cultural Centre first, then the business visa.

research.route: Authority to Work or Study while on a Visitors Permit (up to 12 weeks)
research.detail: Research is one of the activities allowed on a visitors permit with this authority, for up to 12 weeks from arrival.
research.next: Apply for the authority with the research plan.
